newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots mixed.

text.p: -- Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai ended down on Thursday due to a falling domestic A share market, which pushed funds back to the repo market, traders said.
Turnover rose to 8.67 million lots from 6.96 million on Wednesday. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell to 11.99 percent from 14.00 percent.
"Heavy losses on the A share market pushed many funds back to the repo market," said one trader. "Even a new share issue today could not prevent the repo contract falling."

But many traders think the short-term contracts will remain at current levels in the next few days due to more new A share issues, which will lead to increased demand for funds on the repo market, traders said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai closed mixed on Thursday and traders said contracts were likely to find support shortly after successive falls since early this month.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in 2006 ended at 120.57 yuan, up from 120.48 yuan on Wednesday.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 1.78 million lots from 2.17 million.
